acceptance: When review record refuses after the node and model resolve (any later refusal: notes validation, roster role, signing, the approve rules), it writes work/reviews/<NODE_ID>/REJECTED-<model>.md with front matter commit and refused_at and the refusal message as the body (new specy_road/review_rejected.py; review_cli.py stays within 400 lines); a successful review record for that model deletes it; review_files never reads it as a record (its name does not match REVIEW-*.md), pinned by a test

review list and handoff status (text and --json) show, for a model with a REJECTED-<model>.md at the commit under review and no REVIEW-<model> filed at that commit, 'record refused <age> ago: <first line of the refusal>' (JSON key refused with age and reason), through review_run_status.py; a marker at another commit is not shown

Because review delegate and prompt --channel cli --run file through review record (review_record_write._review_record), their refusals write the same marker; tests: a CLI refusal writes it, a later filing removes it, and a delegated refusal writes it. Out of scope: refusals before the node or model resolve (unknown node, a model not in the roster), and what a reviewer says in chat
nodes.title: A refused review record leaves a trace: review record writes REJECTED-<model>.md, and review list and handoff status show it until a record is filed

acceptance: role_prompt_rca.py holds one TEST_RULES tuple of three sentences: no test imports or patches a _-prefixed name or asserts mock call counts, call order or log text no caller relies on; extend or parametrize an existing test before adding one, and add one only for a distinct regression; never weaken, rewrite or delete a failing behavioural test. executor_preamble carries them under 'Tests:' after its step 3, and the reviewer's excess checklist builds its test bullets from the same strings

A test builds an executor prompt and a reviewer prompt for one leaf and asserts each TEST_RULES sentence appears in both. Out of scope: reading the project's agent rule files at prompt time, and project-specific test rules

acceptance: In review_record_rules._second_observation, a part that _parts joins with ',' or ' and ' counts as a separate observation only when _named_defect finds a defect word in that part. Otherwise it belongs to the same observation. When such a part does name a defect, the first part counts as an observation from two words (today three), so one explanation still cannot cover a second part that names a defect. Parts joined by ';', a sentence end or the other _PARTS conjunctions (' but ', ' while ', ' although ' ...) keep today's rule: a defect word, or three words or more that do not open with a _CONTINUES word

note_problem accepts 'No internal imports, mock assertions or defensive branches were added; not a defect because the change uses the existing exclusion mechanism.' and 'The test drives the CLI and checks both the pass case and the fail case, which is not a defect because it is the exact scenario A2 describes.' It still refuses 'X fails and Y crashes; not a defect because the fallback handles both.' with 'says "crashes", two observations joined by "and"', and the comma form 'X fails, Y crashes; ...' with 'joined by ","'

Those rows are added to the existing test_clause_problem or test_note_problem parametrize tables, with no new test functions. Every existing row in tests/test_review_record_rules.py passes unchanged except one: 'The cache miss is expected and the cache key ignores the branch name, not a defect because it is handled.' now expects None. That is the only planned test change; a prototype of the rule fails no other row

PROBE_RULES_LINES rule 4 says a comma or 'and' joins a second observation only when the part after it names a defect; test_reviewer_prompt_carries_the_four_probe_rules still passes. Out of scope: the _DEFECT word list, clause splitting in clause_problem (_CLAUSE_END), the reason check, and sr/tools/review-addendum.md
nodes.title: Review notes: a part joined by a comma or 'and' is a second observation only when it names a defect

acceptance: roadmap_edit_fields defines CODENAME_MAX_CHARS = 64, and every codename derived from a title is capped at that length, including any -<hex> collision suffix. This covers roadmap_crud_prepare.derive_codename_with_collision_suffix, validate_self_heal._derive_codename and maybe_sync_codename_from_title. The cap keeps whole title words, cuts a first word longer than 64 at 64, and never leaves a trailing '-'. title_to_codename's uncapped result stays the same for validate_unique_title_slugs. codename_was_derived accepts both the capped and the uncapped derivation, so an existing long codename still follows title edits

add-node --codename and edit-node --set codename=<value> refuse a value longer than 64 characters with one line, 'error: codename is <n> characters; the limit is 64 (it names feature/rm-<codename> and the planning file)', exit 1 and write nothing. validate does not refuse a node whose codename is already longer, and neither does an edit that does not set codename

planning_artifacts.planning_filename_for_node raises ValueError naming the node when the file name, including the node_key and .md, would be longer than 255 bytes (NAME_MAX), so add-node reports an 'error:' line instead of an OSError. The codename row in docs/roadmap-authoring.md states the 64-character cap

Tests extend the add-node tests in tests/test_roadmap_crud_atomicity.py or tests/test_roadmap_crud_edit_add_remove.py: add-node with a 300-character title and no --codename exits 0, the codename has at most 64 characters and is a word-boundary prefix of the uncapped derivation, and the planning sheet exists with a name of at most 255 bytes. A 65-character --codename is refused and the roadmap files are unchanged. Out of scope: renaming existing long codenames, brainstorm slugify, and branch-name limits beyond the codename
nodes.title: add-node caps a title-derived codename at 64 characters so the planning file name fits

acceptance: AtomicWritePlan.commit in specy_road/bundled_scripts/roadmap_chunk_atomic.py rolls back when write() fails part-way, not only when validate fails. Snapshots are taken before the first byte is written, and any exception from write() or validate restores every staged path (chunks, manifest, planning sheets, staged deletions) byte-for-byte, unlinks each staged path that did not exist before, and removes any .<name>.tmp-* file the plan created. The exception is then re-raised

add-node and edit-node (roadmap_crud_ops.cmd_add and cmd_edit) report an OSError from the write as one 'error: <message>' line and exit 1, with no traceback. write_with_routing and write_node_update give every other caller of the plan (GUI add, brainstorm promote, move and remove paths) the same rollback

Tests in tests/test_roadmap_crud_atomicity.py cover three cases. (a) A plan that stages a chunk and a text file with a 300-character name: commit raises OSError, the chunk's bytes are unchanged and no .tmp- file is left. (b) add-node with planning/ replaced by a regular file: exit 1 with an 'error:' line, and every file under roadmap/ (chunks, manifest, registry) is byte-identical to before. (c) edit-node --set title=... with planning/ read-only, so the sheet rename fails: the same result, with the test skipped when run as root
Out of scope: the self-heal pass that runs before a mutation (heal_before_mutation writes outside the plan by design), git commits, and making scaffold-planning transactional
nodes.title: A roadmap write that fails part-way restores every file it changed

acceptance: finish-this-task writes stdout line-buffered, or flushes stdout before each stderr message, so that when stdout and stderr share one pipe the land check's output comes before the outcome. After a passing land check, the last thing finish prints is either '[ok] merged ...' or one 'error: could not land merge to <ib>: <reason>' line followed by the next command to run

In merge mode (apply_on_complete_mode with on_mode merge, not a rollup), when land_on_integration fails or raises, finish undoes the bookkeeping commit it made in this run. The feature branch goes back to the commit before 'chore(rm-<codename>): complete, deregister' (git reset --keep), and the work files the bookkeeping removed or archived (work/brief-<ID>.md, work/prompt-<ID>.md, work/implementation-summary-<ID>.md) are back at their paths with their original bytes. The error names a plain `specy-road finish-this-task` re-run as the next command. If the undo itself fails, the error says so and names `git reset --keep <sha>`

A branch whose tip is already a bookkeeping commit from an earlier finish still goes through feature_rm_registry to retry_merge_landing as today; its error also prints after all stdout. on_complete auto and pr keep the commit, because the PR needs it. Step 9 of docs/dev-workflow.md and the text of merge_landing_failed describe the new behaviour

Tests run finish-this-task in a sandbox with a bare remote and a passing land check, with stdout and stderr merged into one pipe. (a) A pre-receive hook in the bare remote rejects the push: exit 1, the last 'error:' line comes after the land check output and names the reason ('remote rejected'), the feature branch tip equals its pre-finish sha, the branch's registry still holds the claim, and work/brief-<ID>.md exists. (b) specy_road.finish_modes.land_on_integration is patched to raise OSError: the same guarantees, with the exception text in the error
Out of scope: retrying a transient push failure automatically, the milestone rollup path, and the coordinator scripts under sr/tools
nodes.title: finish-this-task: a failed merge landing reports after the land check output and undoes its bookkeeping commit
